usage.preposition: Beneath normally takes a complement in expressions such as beneath the floor or beneath her.
usage.adverb: In the more literary adverb use, the reference point is understood: a bench with drawers beneath.
usage.register: For literal position, beneath often sounds more formal or literary than under. For numerical thresholds, use under or below, as in below zero.

en: (preposition) at a lower level than something, often directly under it or covered by it
(preposition, figurative) hidden behind an outward appearance
(preposition, figurative) below the level, status, or standards considered appropriate for someone
(adverb) below or underneath, with the reference point understood
ja: （前置詞）〜の下に、〜の真下に、〜に覆われたところに
（前置詞・比喩）表面に見えるものの裏に
（前置詞・比喩）〜の水準に満たない、〜の立場や品位にふさわしくない
（副詞）下に、その下に

nuance.ja: 位置を表す beneath は描写的で、beneath the surface のように表面に隠れたものを描くときにも合う。I thought the work was beneath me. なら、仕事を自分の地位や能力に見合わないと見下している響きが出やすい。That remark was beneath you. なら、相手ならもっと品位ある振る舞いができたはずだという非難や失望を表す。
nuance.en: Beneath lends itself to descriptive writing, especially for things hidden by a surface or an outward appearance. I thought the work was beneath me can sound self-important. That remark was beneath you expresses disappointment that someone acted below the standard you expect of them.

en: under: The everyday choice for physical position. It also appears in expressions such as under pressure and under 18.
below: Common for a lower position or a point on a scale, as in below zero or below average. Beneath often evokes a layer or surface above.
underneath: Often emphasizes direct position or concealment. Beneath also has the established sense of being below someone’s dignity or standards.
ja: under：位置を表す日常的な語。under pressure（プレッシャーを受けて）や under 18（18歳未満）にも使う。
below：位置や数値・基準が低いことに使いやすい。below zero は「零度未満」。beneath には上に覆うものや表面があるイメージが出やすい。
underneath：真下にあることや覆われていることを強調しやすい。beneath には、地位や品位にふさわしくないという用法もある。

note.ja: 物理的に下にある、下に隠れている。
note.en: Physically under or hidden by something.

note.ja: 人の品位や水準にふさわしくない。
note.en: Below the standard someone is expected to meet.

etymology.ja: 中英語 binethe を経て、古英語 beneoðan「下に、より低いところに」にさかのぼる。be- と neoðan「下に」からなり、underneath にも同じ neoðan が含まれる。地位や程度の低さを表す比喩も古英語に見られる。
etymology.en: Through Middle English binethe, from Old English beneoðan, formed with be- and neoðan ‘below.’ The latter element also occurs in the ancestor of underneath. Figurative use for lower rank or degree already existed in Old English.

patterns: come with + included item or service

usage.complement: In these uses, with is followed by a noun or an object pronoun such as me, us, or them: Come with me.
usage.inclusion: The main item is the subject: The camera comes with a charger. You can also make the accessory the subject by saying The charger comes with the camera.

en: to accompany someone to a place or event
to be supplied or included with something, or to have something as part of a package
to have a benefit, risk, obligation, or other consequence associated with it
ja: 人と一緒に来る、ついて行く
（商品・サービスなどに）付属する、セットに含まれる
（役割・選択などに）利点・リスク・責任などが伴う

nuance.ja: Come with me. は、話し手と一緒に移動するよう誘う言い方で、日本語では「ついてきて」「一緒に行こう」とも訳せる。商品やプランを主語にすると、何が付いてくるかを表す。Does it come with breakfast? は、料金やプランに朝食が含まれるかを尋ねる言い方。抽象的な主語では、何かを選んだり引き受けたりすると付いてくるものを表し、責任や費用にも、利点や自由にも使える。
nuance.en: Come with me invites the listener to join the speaker. With a product or plan as the subject, come with says what is provided as part of it. With a role or decision as the subject, it introduces associated consequences, which may be favorable or unfavorable.

en: go with someone: Also means accompany someone. The choice between come and go depends on the speaker’s or listener’s viewpoint.
include: Directly states what forms part of a package or price. Come with often makes an accompanying item or feature the focus.
come along with someone: Often used for joining someone on an outing. Come with also works for items or risks associated with something.
entail: A more formal verb that presents a consequence or requirement as following from an action. Come with is conversational and also works for benefits.
ja: go with someone：人と一緒に行く。come と go は、誰の視点から移動を捉えるかで選ぶ。
include：料金やセットに何が含まれるかを直接述べる。come with は一緒に付いてくる品物や機能に焦点が当たりやすい。
come along with someone：人と連れ立って行く。come with は付属品や、何かに伴うリスクについても使える。
entail：ある行為に結果や条件が伴うことを示す改まった動詞。come with は日常的で、特典や利点にも自然に使える。

note.en: A more formal option for going with someone.
note.ja: 人に同行するという、より改まった言い方。

note.en: A direct way to say something is supplied as part of a package.
note.ja: セットや料金に含まれることを直接表す。

etymology.en: The phrase combines come, a verb of movement, with with, which expresses accompaniment. The same construction extends from someone coming with a companion to an item or consequence being present with something else.
etymology.ja: 移動を表す come と、同伴を表す with の組み合わせ。人が連れ立って来るという発想が、品物が一緒に提供されたり、ある選択に結果が伴ったりする用法にも広がっている。

patterns: in the ordinary course of + noun

usage.article: Ordinary starts with a vowel sound, so use an before a singular countable noun: an ordinary day.
usage.idioms: No ordinary X emphasizes that X is exceptional. Out of the ordinary means unusual. In the ordinary course of business means as part of regular business operations.

en: usual or familiar in character, without any special or unusual features
having no special status or distinction, especially of people or members of a group
ja: ごく普通の、ありふれた、特に変わったところのない
（人や集団について）特別な地位や名声を持たない、一般の

nuance.en: Ordinary is often neutral, as in an ordinary working day or ordinary people. With things such as a film, a meal, or a performance, it can sound mildly dismissive: nothing stood out. No ordinary performance reverses that implication and suggests something exceptional.
nuance.ja: an ordinary working day は「ごく普通の仕事の日」、ordinary people は「一般の人々」で、どちらも中立的に使える。映画や料理について It was pretty ordinary. と言うと、「これといって印象に残らなかった」と控えめに評価を下げる響きが出る。no ordinary performance なら「並の公演ではない」と特別さを強調する。

en: normal: Fits an expected standard, range, or state, as in a normal test result. Ordinary often emphasizes a lack of special features.
usual: Happens regularly for a particular person or situation, as in my usual seat. An ordinary seat describes an unremarkable seat.
common: Widespread or frequent, as in a common mistake. Ordinary describes something’s character as familiar or unremarkable.
average: Can refer to a calculated mean or a middle level of quality. Ordinary often means simply unremarkable.
ja: normal：予想される状態や範囲に収まる。a normal test result は「正常な検査結果」。ordinary は特別さがないことに焦点がある。
usual：人や状況ごとの「いつもの」。my usual seat は「いつもの席」、an ordinary seat は「ごく普通の席」。
common：「よく見られる・頻繁に起こる」。a common mistake は「よくあるミス」。ordinary は目立つ特徴のない普通さを表す。
average：計算上の平均や、中くらいの水準。ordinary は特に目立つものがないという意味でも使う。

note.en: Having nothing that attracts notice.
note.ja: 特に目立つところがない。

note.en: Typical of daily life or used regularly.
note.ja: 日常の、普段使いの。

etymology.en: Middle English ordinarie came through Old French and also draws directly on Latin ordinarius, meaning regular or customary, from ordo, ‘order’ or ‘arrangement.’ The idea of following the usual order developed into the sense of being unexceptional.
etymology.ja: 中英語 ordinarie は古フランス語を経由し、ラテン語 ordinarius「定まった順序に従う、通例の」にさかのぼる。語根は ordo「順序、配列」。通常の順序や慣行に沿うという意味から、特別なところがないという意味にも広がった。

I checked the latest figures and found nothing out of the ordinary. — 最新の数字を確認したが、特に変わった点はなかった。
It looked like an ordinary notebook, but it contained all of her original sketches. — ごく普通のノートに見えたが、彼女のスケッチの原画がすべて収められていた。

usage.register: Uncommon in current English. It still occurs in modern writing, sometimes as a deliberate contrast with ordinary. Unusual is the usual choice for everyday descriptions.
usage.article: Use an before a singular countable noun: an unordinary day.

en: (uncommon) unlike what is usual or typical
(uncommon) distinctive or original enough to stand out
ja: （まれ）普通と違う、いつもと異なる、珍しい
（まれ）ありふれていない、独自性がある、ひと味違う

nuance.en: In contemporary writing, unordinary can call attention to a contrast with ordinary, especially when both words appear close together. It can describe something merely atypical or something distinctive in an appealing way. The word alone does not suggest that the thing is exceptionally good.
nuance.ja: 現代でも使われるが、頻度は低い。ordinary と並べて「いつもどおり」と「いつもとは違う」を際立たせるような文章で使える。単に珍しいという意味にも、独自性を評価する意味にもなり、どちらかは文脈で決まる。

en: unusual: The everyday choice when something departs from what is expected or typical.
out of the ordinary: A familiar phrase for something noticeably different from everyday experience. It is natural after something or nothing.
extraordinary: Often stronger, suggesting something remarkably unusual, impressive, or exceptional.
uncommon: Focuses on how rarely something occurs. Unordinary can also suggest that something has a distinctive character.
ja: unusual：普通と違うことを表す日常的な言い方。
out of the ordinary：日常の範囲から外れた、変わった。something や nothing と組み合わせやすい。
extraordinary：並外れた、驚くほど珍しい、すばらしい。程度の強さを表しやすい。
uncommon：あまり見られない、頻度が低い。unordinary は個性や独自性を指す場合にも使う。

note.en: The everyday equivalent for a departure from what is typical.
note.ja: 「普通と違う」を表す一般的な語。

note.en: A good fit when the point is that something has its own recognizable character.
note.ja: 独自性や、そのものと分かる特徴があることを強調する。

etymology.en: Formed from the negative prefix un- and ordinary. The two parts are still transparent, which makes the word useful for a deliberate contrast with ordinary.
etymology.ja: 否定の接頭辞 un- と ordinary「普通の」を組み合わせた語。語の作りが分かりやすく、ordinary と並べると対比が際立つ。

an unordinary experience

ja: an unordinary day — いつもとは違う一日
an unordinary experience — ひと味違う体験

en: For most of us it was an ordinary Tuesday. For the staff at the little museum, it was a decidedly unordinary day.
She wanted to make something unordinary from the same clay everyone else was using.
The essays find something unordinary in ordinary routines, from making tea to waiting for a bus.
ja: For most of us it was an ordinary Tuesday. For the staff at the little museum, it was a decidedly unordinary day. — 私たちの多くにはいつもどおりの火曜日だった。だが、小さな博物館の職員たちにとっては、明らかにいつもとは違う一日だった。
She wanted to make something unordinary from the same clay everyone else was using. — 彼女はみんなと同じ粘土を使って、ひと味違うものを作りたかった。
The essays find something unordinary in ordinary routines, from making tea to waiting for a bus. — そのエッセイ集は、お茶をいれたりバスを待ったりといった日常の習慣の中に、ありふれていない何かを見つけ出している。

usage.strength: Extraordinary can describe something strikingly good or simply very unusual. The noun and context determine the evaluation.
usage.meetings: An extraordinary meeting is specially convened outside the regular schedule. The expression does not by itself say how urgent the meeting is.

en: very unusual, unexpected, or striking
exceptionally impressive or outstanding
(typically before a noun, especially in formal contexts) outside a regular schedule or procedure
ja: 極めて異例の、驚くほど珍しい、常識では考えにくい
並外れた、目を見張るほどすばらしい
（主に名詞の前・改まった文脈）定例や通常の枠外の、臨時の、特別の

nuance.en: An extraordinary achievement usually expresses admiration. An extraordinary coincidence expresses surprise, and extraordinary damage stresses severity. In institutional language an extraordinary meeting is a meeting outside the regular schedule.
nuance.ja: an extraordinary achievement なら功績への称賛、an extraordinary coincidence なら偶然への驚き、extraordinary damage なら被害の大きさが伝わる。会議については、extraordinary meeting で定例とは別に開く「臨時会議」を指す。

en: ordinary: Regular or unremarkable. Extraordinary marks something well outside the ordinary range or schedule.
unusual: Different from what is normal or expected. Extraordinary typically signals stronger surprise or a greater departure.

unordinary: An uncommon word for something atypical or distinctive, sometimes used in deliberate contrast with ordinary. Extraordinary is the more established choice for something strikingly exceptional.
exceptional: Often emphasizes outstanding quality, although it can also mean outside the norm. Extraordinary readily expresses surprise at an event or coincidence.
ja: ordinary：ごく普通の、通常の。extraordinary は通常の範囲や定例の枠から大きく外れることを示す。
unusual：普通と違う、珍しい。extraordinary は驚きや異例さをより強く伝えることが多い。
unordinary：普通と違う、ひと味違う。ordinary と対比させる文章などに見られるまれな語。並外れたことを表す定着した語は extraordinary。
exceptional：飛び抜けた質を示すことが多く、例外的という意味もある。extraordinary は出来事や偶然への驚きも表しやすい。

note.en: Striking enough to attract attention or admiration.
note.ja: 注目や称賛に値する、目を見張る。

note.en: Close in the sense of exceptional quality or achievement.
note.ja: 質や成果をほめるときの「傑出した」。

etymology.en: From Latin extraordinarius, from extra ordinem, meaning ‘outside the usual order.’ Extra means ‘outside’ and ordinem is a form of ordo, ‘order’ or ‘rank,’ the same root behind ordinary.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 extraordinarius に由来し、extra ordinem「通常の秩序の外に」にさかのぼる。extra は「外に」、ordinem は ordo「順序・階級」の語形で、ordinary と同じ語根を持つ。

an extraordinary coincidence

extraordinary circumstances
an extraordinary general meeting (EGM)

an extraordinary coincidence — 驚くほどの偶然

grammar.countability: plural in form, usually used without an indefinite article

usage.form: The meal name normally appears without a or an. Say have elevenses or have our elevenses. The final -es is pronounced /ɪz/. Some dictionaries treat it as a plural noun and others as uncountable.

en: (British, informal) a mid-morning break, around eleven, for tea or coffee and often a small snack
the drink and light food taken at that break
ja: （英・口語）午前11時ごろにお茶やコーヒーを飲み、軽く何かをつまむ休憩
その休憩でとる飲み物や軽食

nuance.en: A distinctly British name for a small refreshment break between breakfast and lunch. Eleven o’clock is approximate. Tea and biscuits fit the image, but coffee or a different snack works just as well. It can sound traditional or playful.
nuance.ja: 朝食と昼食の間のお茶休憩を指す、英国らしい言い方。11時は目安で、紅茶とビスケットがよく似合うが、コーヒーや別の軽食でもよい。昔ながらの習慣を思わせたり、冗談めかして使われたりする。

en: a mid-morning snack: A neutral description of something eaten between breakfast and lunch. Elevenses can name the whole break, including a drink.
a coffee break: A brief break for coffee or another drink at any time of day. Elevenses places it in late morning.
brunch: A more substantial late-morning meal that often takes the place of breakfast and lunch.
ja: a mid-morning snack：午前中の軽食を指す中立的な言い方。elevenses は飲み物を含めた休憩全体も指せる。
a coffee break：時間帯を問わない短い休憩。elevenses は午前の遅めの時間帯を表す。
brunch：朝食と昼食を兼ねることが多い、しっかりした食事。

note.en: A plain description of the break itself.
note.ja: 午前中のお茶休憩を直接表す。

note.en: A close equivalent when referring to the food.
note.ja: 食べるものに焦点を当てた言い方。

etymology.en: From dialectal elevens, a name for a meal taken at eleven o’clock, with a further plural ending. The name preserves the time of the traditional break.
etymology.ja: 「11時の食事」を指した方言形 elevens に、さらに複数語尾が付いた形。休憩をとる時刻が名前の由来になっている。

usage.adjectives: Fascinating describes what holds your attention. Fascinated describes how you feel: I was fascinated by the talk. The talk was fascinating.

en: extremely interesting and able to hold someone’s attention
ja: 非常に興味深い、強く興味を引く、引き込まれるほど面白い

nuance.en: Fascinating expresses stronger interest than interesting. It fits a subject you want to learn more about, a process you cannot stop watching, or a detail that makes you reconsider what you knew. The topic can be unsettling as well as enjoyable.
nuance.ja: interesting よりも強く興味を引かれ、もっと知りたい、もっと見ていたいと感じるときに使う。知的な関心を引く話にも、見入ってしまう作業にも合う。題材が不気味でも、強く引きつけられるなら fascinating と言える。

en: interesting: A broad, milder description of something that draws interest.
fascinated: Describes the person who feels strong interest. Fascinating describes what sparks it.
intriguing: Arouses curiosity, often because something is puzzling or unexpected. Fascinating emphasizes how strongly it holds your interest.
captivating: Holds attention by being absorbing or charming, especially in a story or performance. Fascinating also fits a fact or an explanation.
ja: interesting：幅広く使える「興味深い」。fascinating は、より強く心を引かれることを示す。
fascinated：強く興味を引かれている人の状態。fascinating はその興味を引き起こすものを表す。
intriguing：謎や意外な点があって好奇心をそそる。fascinating は興味を強く引きつけることに焦点がある。
captivating：物語や演技などが魅力的で、心を奪われる。fascinating は事実や説明など、知的な関心を引くものにも使いやすい。

note.en: Engaging enough to keep your attention for some time.
note.ja: 夢中になって見たり読んだりできるほど面白い。

note.en: Makes you curious to find out more.
note.ja: もっと知りたいと思わせる、好奇心をそそる。

etymology.en: The adjective comes from the -ing form of fascinate. The verb came through French fasciner from Latin fascinare, ‘to bewitch.’ The idea of holding someone under a spell developed into holding someone’s attention.
etymology.ja: 動詞 fascinate の -ing 形からできた形容詞。動詞はフランス語 fasciner を経て、ラテン語 fascinare「魔法をかける」にさかのぼる。魔法にかけて相手をとらえるという意味から、注意や関心を強く引きつける意味に広がった。

a fascinating insight into something
find something fascinating
absolutely fascinating

The documentary was unsettling at times, but I found it fascinating. — そのドキュメンタリーには時折ぞっとするところもあったが、私はとても興味を引かれた。

patterns: have a profound effect / impact on + noun

usage.collocations: Use into with insight and on with effect or impact. Profound is mainly figurative in everyday modern English.

en: showing deep understanding or thought
having a very strong or far-reaching effect, or involving fundamental change
felt or experienced very intensely
ja: 深い理解や思考を示す、洞察の深い
非常に大きな影響を及ぼす、根本に及ぶ
（感情などが）非常に強い、深く感じられる

nuance.en: A profound insight reaches beyond surface observations. A profound impact can change how people live or think. With emotions, profound conveys depth or intensity, as in profound grief or a profound sense of relief. It is often more formal than deep.
nuance.ja: a profound insight は表面的な観察を超えた「深い洞察」。a profound impact は人の暮らしや考え方にまで及ぶような「大きな影響」。profound grief や a profound sense of relief は感情の深さや強さを表す。deep より改まった響きが出やすい。

en: deep: A broad word for physical or figurative depth. It works naturally in a deep lake as well as deep sadness.
significant: Important or noticeable enough to matter. A profound impact suggests a particularly strong or far-reaching influence.
insightful: Shows perceptive understanding. Profound often suggests greater depth or implications and also describes strong feelings or effects.
ja: deep：物理的な深さにも比喩にも使える。a deep lake（深い湖）や deep sadness（深い悲しみ）など。
significant：無視できないほど重要な、顕著な。a profound impact は、影響の強さや及ぶ範囲をより強く示す。
insightful：物事の本質をよく見抜いている。profound は理解の深さを強く示すほか、感情や影響にも使える。

note.en: A close equivalent for feelings or understanding.
note.ja: 感情や理解についての「深い」。

note.en: Emphasizes effects that extend widely.
note.ja: 影響が広い範囲に及ぶ。

etymology.en: From Old French profont or profund and Latin profundus, ‘deep,’ formed from pro ‘forth’ and fundus ‘bottom.’ Both literal depth and figurative depth were already expressed in Latin.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 profont / profund とラテン語 profundus「深い」にさかのぼる。ラテン語では pro「前へ」と fundus「底」から成り、物理的な深さと比喩的な深さの両方に使われた。

en: a profound insight into something
have a profound impact on something
profound changes
a profound sense of relief
be profoundly affected by something
ja: a profound insight into something — ある物事についての深い洞察
have a profound impact on something — 何かに大きな影響を与える
profound changes — 根本に及ぶ変化
a profound sense of relief — 心の底からの安堵
be profoundly affected by something — 何かに深く影響を受ける

en: Her research offers a profound insight into why people resist changes that would make their work easier.
The shift to remote work had a profound impact on how new colleagues got to know one another.
I felt a profound sense of relief when the missing notebook turned up.
The invention brought about profound changes in how people shared information.
ja: Her research offers a profound insight into why people resist changes that would make their work easier. — 彼女の研究は、仕事が楽になるはずの変化になぜ人が抵抗するのかについて、深い洞察を与えてくれる。
The shift to remote work had a profound impact on how new colleagues got to know one another. — 在宅勤務への移行は、新しい同僚同士がどうやって親しくなるかに大きな影響を与えた。
I felt a profound sense of relief when the missing notebook turned up. — なくしたノートが見つかったとき、心の底からほっとした。
The invention brought about profound changes in how people shared information. — その発明は、人々が情報を共有する方法を根本から変えた。

patterns: be profoundly affected / moved by + noun
be profoundly grateful to someone for something

usage.placement: It usually goes before what it modifies: profoundly different, profoundly affected, or profoundly changed the way we work.

en: to a very great degree, especially in a way that involves deep feeling, a marked difference, or fundamental change
ja: 深く、心の底から、極めて、根本から（感情・違い・変化などを強調する）

nuance.en: Profoundly grateful emphasizes the depth of gratitude. Profoundly different suggests a difference of real substance. With verbs like change, profoundly can signal a change that reaches the foundations of how something works. It often sounds more emphatic or formal than deeply.
nuance.ja: profoundly grateful は「心から感謝している」、profoundly different は「根本的に異なる」、profoundly change は「根本から変える」と、組み合わせに応じて訳せる。単なる程度の高さに加え、感情や影響が深いところに及ぶ感じがあり、deeply より改まった響きが出ることがある。

en: deeply: A close match with emotions and reactions, as in deeply moved. It also describes physical actions, such as breathe deeply.
very: A general intensifier before adjectives and adverbs. Profoundly is more selective and can modify verbs in phrases such as profoundly changed our lives.
fundamentally: Emphasizes underlying nature or principles. It overlaps in fundamentally different, while profoundly also fits feelings such as gratitude or grief.
significantly: Emphasizes a noticeable or meaningful degree of change. Profoundly often suggests that the effects go deeper.
ja: deeply：deeply moved のように感情や反応を表すときは近い。breathe deeply（深呼吸する）のような物理的動作にも使う。
very：形容詞や副詞を幅広く強める。profoundly は組み合わせを選ぶが、profoundly changed our lives のように動詞も修飾する。
fundamentally：物事の根本や原則に焦点がある。fundamentally different では意味が重なる。profoundly は感謝や悲しみなどの感情にも使える。
significantly：無視できないほどの違いや変化を表す。profoundly はその影響が深いところに及ぶときに合う。

note.en: A close equivalent for strong feelings and reactions.
note.ja: 感情や反応についての「深く」。

note.en: A neutral paraphrase for the degree of an effect or difference.
note.ja: 影響や違いの程度の大きさを直接表す。

etymology.en: Formed from the adjective profound and the adverb suffix -ly. Profound ultimately goes back to Latin profundus, ‘deep,’ used for both literal and figurative depth.
etymology.ja: 形容詞 profound に、副詞を作る接尾辞 -ly が付いた形。profound はラテン語 profundus「深い」にさかのぼり、物理的な深さと比喩的な深さの両方を表していた。

en: profoundly grateful

ja: I’m profoundly grateful to everyone who made time to read the draft. — 草稿を読む時間を作ってくれた皆さんに、心から感謝しています。
She was profoundly affected by the year she spent teaching abroad. — 彼女は海外で教えた1年間の経験に、深い影響を受けた。

Working from home has profoundly changed the way our team trains new staff. — 在宅勤務によって、私たちのチームでの新人の育て方が根本から変わった。

usage.noun: Use outreach for the activity and a countable noun for a specific initiative or message: an outreach campaign, an outreach email.
usage.verb: Use reach out to someone for the action of making contact.

en: organized efforts to bring information, support, or services to people in the community
proactive contact with a target group, such as potential customers, partners, or stakeholders
ja: 地域の人々に情報・支援・サービスを届けるための活動、訪問支援や普及活動
見込み客や提携先、関係者などにこちらから連絡し、働きかけること

nuance.en: Outreach emphasizes going to people or initiating contact. In public services it can involve taking advice or care into the community. In business it often means contacting selected prospects or partners to start a conversation. An outreach email can be a first contact or part of a broader campaign.
nuance.ja: 相手が来るのを待つのではなく、組織や担当者の側から出向いたり、連絡を取ったりすることに焦点がある。公共サービスでは地域に出向く相談・支援活動などを指し、ビジネスでは見込み客や提携候補との接点をつくる働きかけを指す。

en: reach out to: A verb phrase for contacting someone or offering help. Outreach names the effort or activity.
engagement: Can include ongoing participation and two-way interaction. Outreach is often the effort to establish contact or access.
publicity: Seeks public attention or coverage. Outreach is often directed at particular groups and can deliver services as well as information.
ja: reach out to：人に連絡したり、支援を申し出たりする動作。outreach はその活動を指す。
engagement：継続的な参加や双方向の関わりも含む。outreach は接点をつくったり、支援を届けたりする働きかけに焦点がある。
publicity：世間の注目や報道を得る活動。outreach は特定の対象に向けられることが多く、情報に加えてサービスも届ける場合がある。

note.en: A direct description of initiating contact with others.
note.ja: こちらから積極的に連絡を取ること。

note.en: The expression for outreach directed at people in the community.
note.ja: 地域社会を対象とした支援・普及活動。

etymology.en: The noun comes from reach out, originally the action of extending something outward. The image of reaching out became a way to describe an organization taking its information or services into the community.
etymology.ja: 名詞 outreach は、外に向かって手を伸ばすことを表す reach out に由来する。そこから、組織が地域へ出向いて情報やサービスを届ける活動を指すようになった。

equivalents.fr: action de proximité / prise de contact proactive
equivalents.es: labor de acercamiento a la comunidad / contacto proactivo

an outreach program
outreach to local businesses
sales outreach
an outreach email

usage.place: At the pawnbroker’s means at the pawnbroker’s shop.

en: a person or business that lends money against personal property left as security
ja: 質屋、質屋業者。品物を質に取って金を貸す人や業者

nuance.en: The item stays with the pawnbroker as security for the loan. The borrower can get it back by repaying the loan and any agreed charges. If the borrower fails to repay on time, the pawnbroker may sell the item.
nuance.ja: 預けた品は借入金の担保になる。借入金と取り決められた利息や手数料などを支払えば、品物を取り戻せる。期限までに返済しない場合、質屋は品物を売却できることがある。

en: pawnshop: The shop where a pawnbroker does business.
secondhand dealer: A dealer who buys and sells used goods. A pawnbroker makes loans against valuables.
pawn (verb): To leave an item as security for a loan.
ja: pawnshop：質屋の店舗。pawnbroker はそこで融資を行う人や業者。
secondhand dealer：中古品を買い取って売る業者。pawnbroker は品物を担保に金を貸す。
pawn（動詞）：品物を質に入れる。

note.en: A term for a lender that offers pawn loans.
note.ja: 質物を担保とする融資を行う業者。

etymology.en: A compound of pawn, meaning an item pledged as security, and broker. Pawn here is the word used in to pawn a watch.
etymology.ja: 担保として預ける品を表す pawn と、取引を扱う人を表す broker の複合語。ここでの pawn は pawn a watch（時計を質に入れる）の pawn と同じ語。

en: a local pawnbroker
borrow money from a pawnbroker
take a watch to a pawnbroker
get a ring back from the pawnbroker

borrow money from a pawnbroker — 質屋からお金を借りる
take a watch to a pawnbroker — 時計を質屋に持ち込む
get a ring back from the pawnbroker — 質屋から指輪を取り戻す

ja: He took his watch to a pawnbroker to borrow enough money to cover the repair bill. — 修理代をまかなうお金を借りるため、彼は腕時計を質屋に持ち込んだ。
She paid off the loan and got her ring back from the pawnbroker. — 彼女は借入金を完済し、質屋から指輪を取り戻した。

grammar.countability: uncountable or singular for an amount; plural excesses for extreme acts or behavior; countable in UK insurance

usage.adjective: Use excess before a noun: excess baggage, excess capacity. Use excessive when you mean that something goes beyond a reasonable limit: The fees are excessive.
usage.pronunciation: The noun can have first- or second-syllable stress in both UK and US English. The adjective has first-syllable stress.

en: (noun) an amount above what is needed, expected, or permitted
(adjective) above what is needed or allowed
(plural noun) acts or behavior that go far beyond what is acceptable
(UK insurance, noun) the part of a claim that the policyholder has to pay
ja: 過剰、余り、超過分
余分な、規定量を超えた（名詞の前に置く）
行き過ぎた行為、度を越した振る舞い
（英・保険）免責金額、保険金請求時の契約者の自己負担額

nuance.en: Excess can point to a surplus or to an amount beyond a set limit. In excess of means more than and is formal. It often appears in reports, contracts, and financial figures and can be neutral. To excess means to an unreasonable degree and typically conveys criticism.
nuance.ja: excess は必要量を超えた余りや、定められた上限を超えた分を指す。in excess of は「〜を超える」というやや硬い表現で、報告書や契約書などで中立的に数値を示せる。to excess は「度を越して」を意味し、行為への批判を含みやすい。

en: excess vs. excessive: Excess capacity is spare capacity beyond current needs. Excessive fees are judged unreasonably high.
excess vs. surplus: Surplus often refers to what is available beyond demand, or a positive balance. Excess can also suggest too much or a limit being exceeded.
in excess of vs. at least: In excess of 100 excludes 100. At least 100 includes it.
excess vs. deductible: The usual US insurance term for a policyholder’s share in this sense is deductible.
ja: excess / excessive：excess capacity は現時点の必要量を上回る余剰能力。excessive fees は高すぎると評価される料金。
excess / surplus：surplus は需要を超えて残るものや収支の黒字によく使う。excess は過剰や上限超過も表せる。
in excess of / at least：in excess of 100 は「100を超える」。at least 100 は「100以上」で、100を含む。
excess / deductible：保険の「免責金額」は、イギリス英語では excess、アメリカ英語では通常 deductible。

note.en: An amount left over beyond what is needed.
note.ja: 必要量を上回る余剰分。

note.en: The everyday equivalent of in excess of before a number.
note.ja: 数値の前に置く in excess of の日常的な言い換え。

etymology.en: From Latin excessus, from excedere ‘to go beyond’. Excess and exceed share the image of going beyond a limit.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 excessus に由来し、そのもとに excedere（越えていく）がある。exceed と同じ語源で、限度を越えるという意味につながる。

equivalents.de: der Überschuss / das Übermaß / die Selbstbeteiligung (Versicherung)

en: an excess of caution
costs in excess of the estimate
drink to excess
excess baggage
excess capacity
trim away excess dough
the excesses of the regime
a voluntary excess
ja: an excess of caution — 慎重すぎること
costs in excess of the estimate — 見積額を超える費用
drink to excess — 度を越して飲酒する
excess baggage — 規定量を超えた手荷物

en: The repairs are expected to cost in excess of £10,000.
After washing the spinach, shake off any excess water.
An excess of stock forced the retailer to cut prices.
He enjoyed a drink but rarely drank to excess.
My car insurance policy has a £250 excess.
ja: The repairs are expected to cost in excess of £10,000. — 修理費は1万ポンドを超える見込みだ。
After washing the spinach, shake off any excess water. — ほうれん草を洗ったら、振って余分な水気を切ってください。
An excess of stock forced the retailer to cut prices. — 在庫が余り、小売業者は値下げを余儀なくされた。
He enjoyed a drink but rarely drank to excess. — 彼は酒が好きだったが、飲みすぎることはめったになかった。
My car insurance policy has a £250 excess. — 私の自動車保険には250ポンドの免責金額が設定されている。

usage.position: Use excessive before a noun (excessive fees) or after a linking verb (the fees seem excessive).
usage.adverb: Use excessively to modify an adjective or adverb: excessively broad, excessively slowly.

en: greater in amount, degree, or intensity than is reasonable, necessary, or appropriate
ja: 過度の、度を越した、必要以上の、過大な

nuance.en: Excessive judges something against a standard, such as what is needed in the circumstances or what most people would consider reasonable. It often conveys criticism. In technical descriptions, the standard may be a practical tolerance, as in excessive vibration. In legal or policy writing, excessive can also express a judgment about proportionality, as in excessive force.
nuance.ja: その場で必要とされる程度や、妥当とされる水準を超えているという判断を含み、批判的な響きを伴うことが多い。excessive vibration（過大な振動）のような技術文では、許容できる範囲を超えることも指す。法律・政策文書での excessive force（過剰な実力行使）のように、状況に照らした相当性が問題になることもある。

en: excess: Excess baggage is baggage above the allowance. Excessive baggage suggests the speaker thinks there is an unreasonable amount.
too much / too many: Everyday ways to make the same judgment. Excessive is more formal and works with both count and noncount nouns.
extreme: Describes a very high degree. Excessive adds that the degree goes beyond what is acceptable or necessary.
exorbitant: Stronger and especially common for prices, fees, or rates.
ja: excess：excess baggage は規定の許容量を超えた手荷物。excessive baggage は手荷物の量が常識的な範囲を超えているという評価を含む。
too much / too many：日常会話でよく使う表現。excessive はやや硬く、可算・不可算のどちらの名詞にも使える。
extreme：程度が極めて高いことを表す。excessive は許容範囲や必要な程度を超えていることまで表す。
exorbitant：より強い表現で、特に値段・料金・料率の法外な高さに使う。

note.en: Common in formal phrases such as undue delay or undue pressure.
note.ja: undue delay（不当な遅延）、undue pressure（不当な圧力）などの硬い表現によく使う。

etymology.en: Part of the same word family as excess and exceed, which ultimately goes back to Latin excedere ‘to go beyond’.
etymology.ja: excess や exceed と同系で、さかのぼるとラテン語の excedere（越えていく）に行き着く。

usage.adjective: Despite the -ly ending, costly is an adjective. In The delay proved costly, costly describes the delay after the linking verb proved.

en: requiring a large amount of money
causing a significant loss or setback
ja: 費用がかかる、高くつく
大きな損失や痛手を招く、代償の大きい

nuance.en: Costly draws attention to the burden or consequences of something. A costly repair takes a lot of money. A costly mistake can cost money, time, an opportunity, or a lead in a game.
nuance.ja: 費用や損失の大きさに焦点がある。a costly repair は修理費がかさむことを表す。a costly mistake の代償には、金銭のほか、時間や機会、試合でのリードなども含まれる。

en: expensive: An expensive watch has a high price. A costly mistake has serious consequences, which may include lost time or a missed opportunity.
excessive: Excessive fees are higher than is reasonable. Costly repairs take a lot of money, even if the price is fair.
damaging: A damaging decision causes harm. A costly decision highlights the loss incurred.
ja: expensive：an expensive watch は値段の高い時計。a costly mistake は代償の大きいミスで、時間や機会を失う場合にも使える。
excessive：excessive fees は妥当な水準を超えた料金。costly repairs は修理費の負担が大きいことを表し、金額自体は妥当な場合にも使える。
damaging：悪影響に焦点がある。costly は被った損失や払った代償を強調する。

note.en: A close equivalent when the cost is monetary.
note.ja: 金銭的な費用について使う場合の類義語。

etymology.en: Formed from the noun cost and the adjective-forming suffix -ly.
etymology.ja: 名詞 cost（費用、代償）に、形容詞を作る接尾辞 -ly が付いた語。

equivalents.de: kostspielig / etwas, das teuer zu stehen kommt

ja: Older lifts can be costly to maintain, especially when replacement parts are hard to find. — 古いエレベーターは、特に交換部品が手に入りにくい場合、維持費がかさむことがある。

patterns: a massive amount of + uncountable noun
a massive number of + plural noun

usage.position: Use massive before a noun (a massive door) or after a linking verb (the impact was massive).
usage.agreement: Say a massive amount of data or a massive number of files.

en: extremely large in physical size, often with an impression of weight or solidity
very large in amount, extent, or degree
ja: 巨大な、どっしりした
莫大な、大規模な、非常に大きな

nuance.en: With a physical object, massive can emphasize bulk or solidity, as in a massive stone pillar. With an event or result, it emphasizes scale: a massive success, massive losses, or a massive increase. It works with both favorable and unfavorable outcomes.
nuance.ja: 物については、a massive stone pillar（巨大な石柱）のように、かさやどっしりした印象を強調できる。出来事や結果については、a massive success（大成功）、massive losses（莫大な損失）、a massive increase（大幅な増加）のように、規模の大きさを強調する。好ましい結果にも好ましくない結果にも使える。

en: huge: Often interchangeable with massive for size or scale. Massive can add an impression of bulk with solid objects.
substantial: Often means sizeable or significant in reports and business writing. Massive makes a stronger claim about scale.
excessive: Excessive spending implies spending beyond a reasonable level. Massive spending emphasizes how much was spent.
costly: A massive project is large in scope. A costly project takes a lot of money or carries a substantial cost.
ja: huge：大きさや規模を表す場合は、多くの文脈で massive と置き換えられる。massive は固い物について、どっしりした印象も出せる。
substantial：報告書やビジネス文書で「相当な、かなりの」を表す。massive は規模の大きさをより強く打ち出す。
excessive：excessive spending は妥当な水準を超えた支出。massive spending は支出額の大きさを強調する。
costly：a massive project は規模の大きな事業。a costly project は費用や負担の大きい事業。

note.en: A close equivalent for exceptional size or amount.
note.ja: 並外れた大きさや量を表す類義語。

note.en: A common equivalent for both physical size and abstract scale.
note.ja: 物の大きさにも抽象的な規模にもよく使う類義語。

etymology.en: Historically related to mass through French massif, which carried senses of solidity and bulk.
etymology.ja: フランス語 massif を経た語で、mass（かたまり）と同系。中身の詰まった固さや、かさの大きさを表す意味があった。

usage.compounds: A hay barn is used to store hay. A dairy barn houses dairy cattle or is used in dairy operations.

en: a farm building, usually fairly large, used to store hay, crops, or equipment or to house animals
ja: 農場の納屋、畜舎。干し草・作物・農機具などを保管したり、家畜を入れたりする建物

nuance.en: Barn describes a type of farm building with several possible uses. The best translation depends on what is inside: a hay barn is a storage building, while a barn full of cows is a livestock building. In barn conversion, the term can refer to either the work or the resulting home, depending on context.
nuance.ja: barn は用途が一つに限られない農場の建物。干し草を保管していれば「納屋」、牛を入れていれば「牛舎」など、中で何をするかに応じて訳し分ける。barn conversion は文脈により、納屋を住宅に改装することや、改装した住宅そのものを指す。

en: shed: A general word for a simple outbuilding, often smaller and used to store tools or garden equipment. A barn typically belongs to a farm.
stable: A building or room where horses are kept. A barn may contain stalls for horses and also have space for hay and equipment.
silo: A structure or container designed for bulk storage, for example of grain or silage.
ja: shed：庭の物置などにも使う広い語で、比較的小さな簡易建物を指すことが多い。barn は典型的には農場の建物。
stable：馬を入れる厩舎。barn には馬房のほか、干し草や機材を置く場所がある場合もある。
silo：穀物やサイレージなどを大量に貯蔵するための設備。

note.en: A broader term that also includes farm sheds and other separate buildings.
note.ja: 農場にある別棟の総称。納屋のほか、物置なども含む。

etymology.en: From Old English bereærn, literally a building for barley, from bere ‘barley’ and ærn ‘house, building’.
etymology.ja: 古英語 bereærn に由来する。bere（大麦）と ærn（建物）からなり、もとは大麦を保管する建物を指した。

usage.verb: As a verb, sled is usually intransitive when it means to ride a sled. Double the d in sledded and sledding.
usage.regional: Sled and go sledding are especially common in North American English. British English commonly uses sledge and go sledging.

en: (noun) a vehicle that slides over snow or ice, used for recreation or to carry people or loads
(verb, especially North American) to ride on a sled, often for fun
ja: そり。雪や氷の上で遊んだり、人や荷物を運んだりする道具・乗り物
（主に北米）そりに乗る、そりで滑る

nuance.en: A sled may be a lightweight toy for sliding downhill or a vehicle pulled by dogs to carry people and supplies. Sleds often have runners, although some modern play sleds slide on a smooth plastic base.
nuance.ja: 坂を滑り降りて遊ぶ軽いそりにも、人や物資を運ぶ犬ぞりにも使える。底に滑走用の細長い部材が付いたものが多いが、遊び用にはプラスチックの底面全体で滑るタイプもある。

en: sledge: The usual British equivalent of sled, for both recreation and transport.
sleigh: Often a larger passenger sled pulled by horses or, in stories, reindeer.
toboggan: Traditionally a long, flat sled with no runners and an upturned front.
ja: sledge：遊び用や運搬用のそりを指す、イギリス英語で一般的な呼び方。
sleigh：馬などが引く比較的大きな人乗りのそりによく使う。サンタのそりも sleigh。
toboggan：伝統的には、先端が反り上がった細長い板状のそり。底に滑走用の細長い部材がない。

note.en: The common British English equivalent.
note.ja: イギリス英語で一般的な相当語。

etymology.en: From Dutch slede ‘sledge’.
etymology.ja: オランダ語の slede（そり）に由来する。

grammar.countability: collective noun with no regular countable singular or plural

usage.counting: Use an animal or a head of livestock for one animal. Use fifty head of livestock to count fifty animals collectively.
usage.agreement: Plural agreement is common when referring to the animals as individuals: The livestock are out in the fields.

en: animals kept for farming, such as cattle, sheep, goats, and pigs
ja: 家畜。牛・羊・ヤギ・豚など、農業や畜産のために飼われる動物の総称

nuance.en: Livestock groups animals by their role in farming. It can cover several species on one farm or all the farm animals in a region. In broad use it can include poultry, while some agricultural classifications list livestock and poultry separately.
nuance.ja: 農場で飼育される動物をひとまとめにする語。農場にいる複数の種類の家畜にも、地域全体の家畜にも使える。広い意味では家禽も含むが、農業統計などの分類では livestock と poultry を別に扱うこともある。

en: cattle: Cows, bulls, and other bovines raised on farms. Livestock is broader and includes animals such as sheep and pigs.
poultry: Domesticated birds such as chickens, ducks, and turkeys kept for their meat or eggs.
farm animals: An everyday phrase for animals kept on a farm. Livestock is common in discussions of farming, trade, and animal health.
ja: cattle：農場で飼われる牛の総称。livestock は羊や豚も含む、より広い語。
poultry：肉や卵を得るために飼うニワトリ、アヒル、七面鳥などの家禽。
farm animals：農場で飼われる動物を指す日常的な表現。livestock は畜産、取引、家畜の衛生管理などの話題でよく使う。

note.en: An everyday near-equivalent.
note.ja: 日常語での近い言い換え。

etymology.en: A compound of live /laɪv/ ‘alive’ and stock in its sense of animals kept on a farm.
etymology.ja: live /laɪv/（生きている）と、農場で飼育される動物を意味する stock の複合語。

The farm keeps about fifty head of livestock, mostly sheep and goats. — その農場では家畜を約50頭飼っており、その大半は羊とヤギだ。

grammar.countability: collective for live birds; uncountable for meat

usage.counting: To count individual birds, use three chickens or three birds, or name the species.
usage.agreement: Plural agreement is possible with live birds (The poultry are kept indoors). Use singular agreement for meat (The poultry is fresh).

en: domesticated birds kept for their meat or eggs, such as chickens, ducks, or turkeys
the meat of these birds, considered as a type of food
ja: 家禽（かきん）。肉や卵を得るために飼うニワトリ、アヒル、七面鳥などの総称
家禽の肉。鶏肉、鴨肉、七面鳥の肉などをまとめた食品の区分

nuance.en: In farming, poultry refers to the birds themselves. In a recipe or on a food label, it usually refers to their meat. A shop sign reading ‘Meat & Poultry’ uses meat in a narrower sense for that grouping.
nuance.ja: 畜産では鳥そのものを指し、レシピや食品表示ではたいていその肉を指す。売り場表示で Meat & Poultry と並んでいれば、その区分では meat が家禽の肉を除く狭い意味で使われている。

en: livestock: The broader category of farm animals. Some farming classifications list livestock and poultry separately.
chicken: One kind of poultry, or its meat. Poultry also covers birds such as ducks and turkeys.
fowl: A word for birds such as chickens and ducks that also occurs in names for wild birds, as in wildfowl.
ja: livestock：家畜の総称。農業の分類によっては livestock と poultry を別の区分にする。
chicken：ニワトリ、または鶏肉。poultry にはアヒルや七面鳥なども含まれる。
fowl：ニワトリやアヒルなどを指す語で、wildfowl のように野生の鳥を指す語にも現れる。

note.en: A plain description of the live-bird sense.
note.ja: 生きた家禽を指す場合の説明的な言い換え。

usage.register: A formal adjective used for people and for works or remarks that display deep learning.

en: having or showing extensive knowledge acquired through study or reading
ja: 博識な、学識の深い。文章や講演については、深い学識がうかがえる

nuance.en: Erudite typically expresses admiration for knowledge gained through study. It works for a person as well as for a work that draws on deep learning. Whether that learning makes the work difficult depends on the context: erudite yet accessible is a natural combination.
nuance.ja: 読書や研究で身につけた深い学識を評価する、やや硬い語。人だけでなく、豊かな知識に裏づけられた本や講演にも使える。学識の深さと読みやすさは両立するので、erudite yet accessible（学識豊かでありながら分かりやすい）とも言える。

en: learned: A close synonym for deep learning. The adjective is pronounced /ˈlɜː.nɪd/ in British English.
knowledgeable: A broader term for knowing a lot about a subject, including through practical experience.
scholarly: Often describes work that uses academic methods or conventions. Erudite emphasizes the depth or breadth of learning on display.
pedantic: Critical of excessive attention to small details or rules. Erudite is usually approving.
ja: learned：深い学識を表す近い類義語。形容詞では二音節で発音する。
knowledgeable：ある分野に詳しいことを表す広い語。実務経験で身につけた知識にもよく使う。
scholarly：学術的な方法や形式を備えた文章・研究にも使う。erudite はそこに表れた学識の深さや幅広さを強調する。
pedantic：細かな規則や知識にこだわりすぎることを批判する語。erudite は通常、学識を評価する語。

note.en: Especially close when describing a person of deep learning.
note.ja: 学識の深い人を形容する場合に特に近い。

etymology.en: From Latin eruditus, the past participle of erudire ‘to educate’. The verb combines ex- ‘out’ with rudis ‘rough, untrained’, the source of English rude.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 erudire（教育する）の過去分詞 eruditus に由来する。erudire は ex-（外へ）と rudis（粗野な、未熟な）からなり、rudis は rude の語源でもある。

en: an erudite scholar
an erudite essay
an erudite account of the period
an erudite discussion
erudite yet accessible
ja: an erudite scholar — 博識な学者
an erudite essay — 学識の深さがうかがえる論考
an erudite account of the period — その時代についての学識豊かな解説
an erudite discussion — 深い学識に裏づけられた議論
erudite yet accessible — 学識豊かでありながら分かりやすい

en: Her book on medieval trade is erudite yet accessible, even to readers who know little about the period.
He was an erudite historian who could move easily from medieval maps to early travel diaries.
The reviewer praised the essay for its erudite discussion of the novel’s historical context.
ja: Her book on medieval trade is erudite yet accessible, even to readers who know little about the period. — 彼女の中世の交易に関する本は、深い学識に裏づけられていながら、その時代に詳しくない読者にも分かりやすい。
He was an erudite historian who could move easily from medieval maps to early travel diaries. — 彼は博識な歴史家で、中世の地図から初期の旅行日記まで、どの話題にも通じていた。

usage.plural: In hypotheses, the last syllable is /siːz/. In hypothesis, it is /sɪs/.
usage.thatClause: A that-clause states the content of the hypothesis: the hypothesis that the delay reduced sales.

en: a provisional explanation or claim that can be investigated or tested against evidence
a supposition adopted as a starting point for reasoning
ja: 仮説。観察やデータなどに照らして検証できる暫定的な説明や主張
推論の出発点として置く仮定

nuance.en: In research, a hypothesis often explains an observation or proposes a relationship that evidence can support or count against. A working hypothesis is the provisional explanation that guides an investigation. In statistics, a null hypothesis is a formal claim assessed by a statistical test. Data may support a hypothesis without settling the question conclusively.
nuance.ja: 研究では、観察された現象の説明や、証拠に照らして評価できる関係性の主張を指すことが多い。working hypothesis（作業仮説）は、調査の手がかりとする暫定的な説明。統計では、null hypothesis（帰無仮説）は検定で評価する形式的な主張を指す。データが仮説を支持しても、それだけで結論が確定するとは限らない。

en: theory: In science, a theory is typically a broad explanatory framework supported by evidence. A hypothesis is often a more specific claim to investigate. In everyday English, theory can also mean a tentative explanation.
assumption: A premise taken as given for the reasoning at hand. A hypothesis is often itself the claim being examined.
prediction: An expected result. A hypothesis can give rise to a prediction about what should happen under particular conditions.
guess: A broader, more conversational word for a tentative judgment, which may be based on very little information.
ja: theory：科学では、証拠に裏づけられた広い説明の枠組みを指すことが多い。hypothesis は調べるべき個別の仮説を指すことが多い。日常語の theory には「こうではないかという考え」の意味もある。
assumption：その推論の出発点として所与とする前提。hypothesis はしばしば、その主張自体が検討対象になる。
prediction：予想される結果。仮説をもとに、一定の条件で何が起こるかを予測できる。
guess：少ない情報でも下せる暫定的な判断を表す、より広く口語的な語。

note.en: A plain-language equivalent when the hypothesis is intended to explain an observation.
note.ja: 観察された現象の説明を試みる仮説の、平易な言い換え。

etymology.en: Ultimately from Greek hypothesis, from hypo- ‘under’ and thesis ‘a placing’. The original image is of something laid down as a basis for reasoning.
etymology.ja: ギリシャ語 hypothesis にさかのぼる。hypo-（下に）と thesis（置くこと）からなり、推論の土台となるものを置くという発想につながる。

en: The team tested the hypothesis that clearer instructions would reduce the number of errors.

ja: The team tested the hypothesis that clearer instructions would reduce the number of errors. — チームは、手順の説明を明確にすればミスが減るという仮説を検証した。
Our working hypothesis is that customers are abandoning the form because it asks for too much information. — 現時点では、入力項目が多すぎるために利用者がフォームの記入を途中でやめていると仮定している。
Both hypotheses fit the initial observations, but they make different predictions. — どちらの仮説も最初の観察結果と整合するが、そこから導かれる予測は異なる。

grammar.countability: countable for an individual explanation or framework; uncountable for principles as a body of knowledge

usage.countability: Use a theory for one explanation (a theory about the delay) and theory without an article for a body of principles (music theory).
usage.idiom: In theory means according to the principles or assumptions involved. It often contrasts with in practice.

en: an organized explanation of how or why something happens
the principles underlying a subject or activity
an idea about what happened or why, especially in everyday speech
ja: 理論。現象の仕組みや理由を体系的に説明するもの
ある分野や活動の基礎となる理論・原理
（日常語）何が起きたか、なぜそうなったかについての見立て、推測

nuance.en: In science, a theory such as plate tectonics organizes evidence and explains a range of observations. In ordinary conversation, I have a theory can introduce an explanation that the speaker has yet to check. In theory, the plan should work signals that the plan looks workable under the stated or assumed conditions, with room for practical complications.
nuance.ja: 科学での theory は、プレートテクトニクスのように、証拠をまとめてさまざまな観察結果を説明する枠組みを指す。日常会話の I have a theory は、まだ確かめていない自分なりの説明を切り出す言い方。In theory, the plan should work は、想定どおりの条件ならうまくいくはずだが、実際には問題が生じる余地もある、という含みを持ちうる。

en: hypothesis: Often a specific, testable claim. A scientific theory typically explains a wider range of observations. In everyday conversation, theory can also refer to a tentative explanation.
model: A representation of a system or process, often simplified. A theory may use several models to explain a phenomenon.
hunch: An intuitive feeling that something is true. A theory offers an account of what happened or why.
ja: hypothesis：多くは検証可能な個別の仮説。科学での theory は、より広い範囲の観察結果を説明する枠組みを指すことが多い。日常語の theory には暫定的な見立ての意味もある。
model：仕組みや過程を表す表現や枠組みで、しばしば単純化されている。一つの theory が現象を説明するために複数の model を用いることがある。
hunch：何かが事実だろうという直感。theory は何が起きたか、なぜそうなったかについての説明を示す。

note.en: A broader word for an account of how or why something happened.
note.ja: 何がどう、なぜ起きたかについての説明を広く指す語。

etymology.en: Through Late Latin theoria, from Greek theōria ‘viewing, contemplation’. The Greek word could refer to looking at something as well as thinking it over.
etymology.ja: 後期ラテン語 theoria を経て、ギリシャ語 theōria（見ること、観想）にさかのぼる。ギリシャ語では物事を眺めることにも、よく考えることにも使われた。

en: The theory of plate tectonics helps explain why earthquakes cluster along certain boundaries.

In theory, the transfer should take ten minutes. In practice, the buses rarely run on time.
She studied music theory to understand how the chords fit together.
ja: The theory of plate tectonics helps explain why earthquakes cluster along certain boundaries. — プレートテクトニクス理論は、なぜ地震が特定の境界付近に集中するのかを説明するのに役立つ。
I have a theory about why nobody uses that entrance. The sign makes it look like it’s for staff only. — なぜ誰もあの入口を使わないのか、私なりの考えがある。あの表示だと、職員専用に見えるんだ。
